name: React Web Application
description: Reference architecture for a typical React + Node.js web application. Fork it or copy the nodes you need into your own project.

diagrams.name: System context
diagrams.description: How users, the React SPA, and supporting platforms relate. Double-click the **React SPA** or **Backend API** to drill into their internals.

nodes.name: End user
nodes.description:
**End user** accessing the app via a modern browser.

- Cold loads land on the CDN.
- Repeat loads hit the service worker first, then network.
- Auth flows redirect through the auth provider.

nodes.name: CDN
nodes.description:
**CDN edge** — caches the SPA bundle, fonts, and images close to the user.

Common options: **Cloudflare**, **Fastly**, **AWS CloudFront**, **Vercel/Netlify edge**.

nodes.name: React SPA
nodes.description:
The **React single-page app** itself. Mounted in the browser, talks to the backend over HTTPS.

Drill in to see the internal layering: entry point → router → state/query → components.

nodes.name: Analytics
nodes.description:
**Product analytics** — page views, custom events, funnels.

Usually pushed via a tiny client SDK, batched and sent to a SaaS such as **PostHog**, **Mixpanel**, **Amplitude**, or **Google Analytics**.

nodes.name: Backend API
nodes.description:
**Backend API** — Node.js service exposing the data and business logic the SPA needs.

Drill in for the internal breakdown: gateway → BFF → domain services → datastores.

nodes.name: Auth provider
nodes.description:
**Identity / auth provider**. Handles sign-up, sign-in, social, MFA, password resets.

Common picks: **Clerk**, **Auth0**, **AWS Cognito**, **Supabase Auth**, **Keycloak**.

Uses OAuth2 + PKCE from the SPA; backend validates the resulting JWT.

nodes.name: Payments
nodes.description: **Payments provider** (Stripe, Adyen, etc.). Backend orchestrates charges via REST; webhook callbacks update the backend on async events.

diagrams.name: Frontend architecture
diagrams.description: Internal layering of the React SPA. Build tooling on the left, runtime composition in the middle, presentation layer on the right.

nodes.name: Vite
nodes.description:
**Vite** — dev server (esbuild) + production build (Rollup). Reads `vite.config.ts`, plugins for React, Tailwind, etc.

Alternatives: **Webpack**, **Turbopack**, **esbuild** standalone.

nodes.name: TypeScript
nodes.description: **TypeScript** — type-checks the codebase at build time via `tsc --noEmit`. Vite uses esbuild for the runtime transform (no type-check), so the TS step runs in parallel.

nodes.name: main.tsx
nodes.description:
**App entry** — `createRoot(...).render(<App />)`.

Mounts the app inside `<React.StrictMode>` in development. Imports global CSS once.

nodes.name: Router
nodes.description:
**React Router v6+** — URL ↔ route mapping.

- `createBrowserRouter` for SPA routing.
- Code-split route components via `lazy(() => import(...))`.
- `useNavigate` / `useLocation` inside components.

nodes.name: Global state store
nodes.description:
**Client-side state** — UI state, selection, transient flags.

Pick one:

- **Zustand** (recommended, simple, hooks-friendly)
- **Redux Toolkit** (richer dev tools)
- **Jotai** / **Recoil** (atomic state)
- **React Context** (for small leaf trees)

nodes.name: Server-state cache
nodes.description:
**Server state** — fetched data + caching + revalidation.

Pick one:

- **TanStack Query** (most ergonomic)
- **SWR**
- **RTK Query** (if Redux Toolkit already in use)
- **Apollo Client** (if GraphQL)

nodes.name: Shared components
nodes.description:
**UI primitives** + composed components used across pages — forms, dialogs, tables, charts.

Keep accessible by default (use a primitive lib like **Radix UI** as the base).

nodes.name: Design system
nodes.description:
**Design tokens + styling** — colours, spacing, typography, dark/light themes.

Common combo: **Tailwind CSS** + **shadcn/ui** generated components, with HSL CSS variables for theme switching.

nodes.name: Page components
nodes.description:
**Route-bound page components** — one per top-level URL.

Keep these *thin*: orchestrate hooks, render shared components, defer logic to services/hooks.

nodes.name: Service worker
nodes.description:
**Service worker** — installable PWA, offline cache, background sync.

Vite has `vite-plugin-pwa` which generates the SW for you.

diagrams.name: Backend architecture
diagrams.description: Node.js API and supporting infrastructure. Requests enter via the gateway, fan out through domain services, and land in the datastores.

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.description:
**Edge router** — TLS termination, rate limiting, request validation, auth header check.

Options: **NGINX**, **Traefik**, **API Gateway (AWS/GCP)**, or a thin Node layer (Fastify) doing the same.

nodes.name: Auth middleware
nodes.description:
**JWT validation + session loading**. Decodes the token from the `Authorization` header, fetches the user context, attaches to the request.

Rejects unauthenticated requests with 401 before they reach business logic.

nodes.name: REST API
nodes.description:
**Public HTTP surface** — typically Fastify or Express. Thin handlers that parse + validate input, then delegate to the BFF.

Validate everything at the boundary (e.g., **Zod** schemas, **TypeBox**).

nodes.name: BFF
nodes.description:
**Backend-For-Frontend** — composes calls across multiple domain services into a single response shape tailored to the UI.

Keeps the SPA from making N round-trips per screen.

nodes.name: Domain services
nodes.description:
**Business logic** — pure functions over the domain model. No HTTP, no Express imports here. Easy to unit-test.

Depend on repositories that abstract the datastore.

nodes.name: Postgres
nodes.description:
**Primary relational store** — the source of truth.

Access via a typed ORM (**Drizzle**, **Prisma**, **Kysely**) or hand-rolled SQL with **node-postgres**.

Use migrations from day one.

nodes.name: Redis
nodes.description:
**Hot cache + session store**.

Useful for: session tokens, rate-limit counters, ephemeral keyspace, pub/sub fan-out, BullMQ backing.

nodes.name: Background jobs
nodes.description:
**Async work** — anything you don't want on the request path.

Options: **BullMQ** (Redis-backed), **Inngest**, **Temporal**, **SQS + workers**.

nodes.name: Object storage
nodes.description:
**Blob storage** — uploads, generated reports, image processing inputs/outputs.

Options: **S3**, **R2**, **GCS**, **Azure Blob**.

tours.name: React web app — guided tour
tours.description: A six-stop walkthrough of the reference architecture, ending at the database that backs it all.

stops.note: **Every flow starts here.** An end user hits a URL in their browser. The first request usually lands on the CDN; subsequent requests go through the React SPA.

The **React SPA** is the entire client surface. It's served as a static bundle and runs in the browser.

Double-click this node any time to drill into its internals — or just continue the tour.

Inside the SPA, the **router** maps URLs to page components.

Keep page components thin: they orchestrate hooks and compose shared components, nothing more.

**Server state vs. client state** is the single most important architectural split in a modern React app.

The **Query cache** owns anything that came from the backend; the **State store** owns anything that lives only in the browser.

We've crossed the network boundary. The **API gateway** is the first thing every request hits — TLS, rate limiting, auth header check.

No business logic here, just policy.

And we land at **Postgres**, the source of truth. Every other store (Redis cache, S3 blobs, the queue) is downstream of this one.

Guard it accordingly: typed access, migrations, backups, observability.
